method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); shared definitions, criteria, the Tribunal's outcomes and seven regulative rules (ss 97(1), 124, 189(1), 204(1), 73/74/90, 76(1), 380(4)) in a rules module, the questions in a seat module importing it; each regulative rule run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

seat: the person the Act is applied to: the person examined for, or made subject to, an assessment order, court assessment order, temporary treatment order or treatment order; a patient asked to consent to treatment, medical treatment, electroconvulsive treatment or neurosurgery; a person in a designated mental health service who may be secluded or restrained; a party before the Mental Health Tribunal; a consumer with a complaint (mhw-seat.l4)

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text and a calendar.

scope: Focus: mental health services, compulsory assessment and treatment, rights, the Mental Health Tribunal. In: s 3(1) (patient, eligible patient, young patient, young person, bodily restraint, restrictive intervention), s 4; Chapter 2 ss 53, 54, 57-59, 62-65, 67, 68, 69(2), 73(2)-(3), 74(3)-(4), 75, 76(1); Chapter 3 ss 85(2), 86, 87(1), 89-93, 94-117, 119-121, 124, 126-128, 132, 137; Chapter 4 ss 142-147, 153-155, 160, 161, 164, 165, 175, 176, 180, 181, 183, 189, 191-194, 200, 204-209, 212, 217, 226, 227; Part 7.5 ss 363(a), 373(1), (8), 374, 376, 380, 383; Part 9.2 ss 431-434. Out: the principles (Parts 1.3-1.6, 3.1; s 10 says they create no rights); the 'as soon as practicable' duties to inform, explain and give copies (no fixed day); the advocacy machinery; reports and notices to courts and others; Part 3.7 considerations, documentation and transport sedation; Chapter 5 (crisis care and control); Chapters 6-18 except the Tribunal procedure, VCAT review and complaint sections named. Reasons in NOTES.md.
